text: In nineteen eleven, someone stole the most famous painting on Earth, and simply walked out with it. His name was Vincenzo Peruggia. He had worked at the Louvre, so he knew its secrets. On a Monday, when the museum was closed, he slipped in wearing a white smock, just like the staff. He lifted the painting off the wall, ditched the frame in a stairwell, and left. Nobody noticed until the next day. For over two years, it hid in a trunk in his Paris apartment. Then he tried to sell it to an art dealer in Florence. The dealer called the museum director, and police arrested him. And the twist? The theft made the Mona Lisa a global superstar. Part two: a man who hijacked a plane, and vanished into the sky.
